questions.question: What does the Socratic tutor policy mean in practice, and why is it pedagogically significant?
options: The tutor always provides the full correct answer immediately to avoid learner frustration
When the learner asks for the answer, the policy asks a leading question rather than giving it; when they get it right, it moves to the next concept; when stuck, it offers a scaffolded hint
The tutor generates multiple-choice questions at random from the curriculum graph
The policy routes hard questions to a human teacher and easy questions to an automated hint system
questions.explanation: The Socratic policy governs how the tutor responds at every interaction point: guide with questions rather than dump answers, scaffolding hints when stuck and advancing when correct, following established pedagogy for deeper learning.

questions.question: What does Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) estimate per concept after each interaction?
options: The probability that the learner's answer was generated by guessing rather than knowledge
The mastery probability per curriculum concept node, updated after each interaction using guess, slip, and learn-rate priors
The semantic similarity between the learner's response and the target correct answer
The number of times a learner has visited a concept node across all sessions
questions.explanation: BKT maintains a per-concept mastery probability for each learner, updating it after every interaction using priors for guess rate, slip rate, and learn rate. This drives the next-concept selection in the tutor policy.

questions.question: How does the curriculum graph structure the subject content and guide the tutor's concept selection?
options: A flat list of concepts ordered by difficulty score assigned by the LLM
A Neo4j graph of concept nodes with prerequisite edges; the policy walks the graph selecting the highest-priority concept the learner is ready for given current mastery
A time-ordered lesson sequence identical for all learners regardless of mastery state
A vector index of OER content chunks that the tutor retrieves based on question similarity
questions.explanation: The curriculum graph is a Neo4j of 50-150 concept nodes with prerequisite edges and attached OER content. The tutor policy walks the graph to select the next concept based on BKT mastery state, enabling adaptive sequencing.

questions.question: What is the COPPA-aware memory retention policy, and what does it require?
options: All learner data is stored encrypted and can only be accessed by the learner after age verification
Episodic interaction records auto-delete after 1 year, parents can request deletion, and memory access is scoped by learner ID
Learner data is anonymized before storage and may be used to train future model versions
Memory is cleared at the end of each session to comply with US children's privacy law
questions.explanation: COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act) applies to users under 13. The retention policy requires auto-deletion after 1 year, a parental access surface for deletion, and learner-ID-scoped memory access to prevent one learner's data from being exposed to another.

questions.question: What is the deliverable measurement from the two-week efficacy study?
options: The percentage of sessions in which the learner completed all assigned exercises without hints
Pre-test and post-test score delta for 10 learners over two weeks, compared against a non-adaptive baseline cohort on the same content
The number of unique concepts each learner mastered as measured by the BKT model
The average voice-session latency and false-cutoff rate across the study period
questions.explanation: The efficacy study measures learning gain: the delta between pre-test and post-test scores for 10 learners over two weeks, compared against a non-adaptive cohort of 10 learners receiving the same content linearly, to isolate the adaptive policy's contribution.

questions.question: What multimodal input channels does this AI tutor support, and what technology handles each?
options: Text (keyboard), audio (WebRTC PCM), video (webcam frames analyzed by a VLM)
Text (web app), voice (LiveKit Agents + Whisper-v3-turbo + Cartesia Sonic-2 TTS), and photo math (dots.ocr or PaliGemma 2 for equation recognition)
Text (web app), voice (Deepgram Nova-3 ASR + ElevenLabs TTS), and sketch (canvas-to-SVG conversion)
Text (chat), voice (GPT-4o-realtime), and screen sharing (OCR on shared screen content)
questions.explanation: The tutor supports typed text via the web app, voice via LiveKit Agents with Whisper-v3-turbo ASR and Cartesia Sonic-2 TTS (reusing the capstone 03 sub-stack), and photo math via dots.ocr or PaliGemma 2 for equation recognition.
